what: The lever that actually reaches 60 tok/s: quantise the dense half
finding: Two thirds of the bytes moved per token are ordinary BF16 attention and MLP weights, not experts. Every optimisation today targeted the expert third. Quantising the dense half to 8 bits takes per-token traffic from 2.568 to 1.714 GB and reaches 37.6 tok/s at the bandwidth we already have, which is 1.66x Strata and 63% of the 60 tok/s goal without any further kernel work.
why_this_is_the_right_next_step: it attacks 67% of the traffic instead of the 33% every change so far addressed
it does not require the bandwidth to double, which five attempts have failed to do
it is the standard post-training quantisation problem, so the tooling exists
it composes with fusion, which is already implemented and measured at 1.98x
risks_stated_up_front: quantising attention hurts quality more than quantising MLP weights, so a per-tensor choice will be needed rather than a blanket 8-bit cast
the dense path has no per-block scale format in this checkpoint, so a new Format is needed, which is what fikra.quant.Formats exists for
quality must be measured on the benchmark slice, and that infrastructure is not built yet - the earlier attempt was void because the manifest carries hashes not text
implemented_today: LayerFootprint.with_dense_bits(4|8|16) and five tests, including one that asserts int8 at our current bandwidth beats Strata. The planner can now compute the gain rather than assert it.
